purpose: Worker profiles used by `route` to pick the least-privilege execution target. The first profile whose hard requirements are satisfied by the requested capabilities wins, scanning in ascending privilege order.

linux-local.description: The current Linux host. Read-only local inspection, builds and packaging that need no Windows, GPU, ARM64, virtualization or network.
linux-local.notes: Default target. Any change still needs an approval record when privileged.

network-enabled-worker.description: The local host with approved outbound network access for downloads, package registries or vulnerability databases.
network-enabled-worker.notes: Never use for production data exfiltration; record every endpoint contacted.

virtualized-worker.description: A VM or sandbox with working KVM/WHPX acceleration for clean-state reproduction, snapshots and untrusted execution.
limits: no shared host folders unless required
virtualized-worker.notes: Preferred place to reproduce failures so the host stays clean.

arm64-worker.description: An ARM64 host or emulated worker for ARM64 and ARM64EC build/test work.
limits: native x86 plugins may be unavailable
arm64-worker.notes: Use only when a capability explicitly requires ARM64.

gpu-worker.description: A worker with a physical GPU for graphics capture, rendering and compute diagnostics.
gpu-worker.notes: Batch GPU work to limit driver restarts.

windows-host.description: A licensed Windows worker with the Windows SDK, WDK and signing tooling.
limits: snapshot or restore point before changes
windows-host.notes: Highest privilege target; dispose of or reimage workers after sensitive jobs.
